commits.edited_message:
Decode the QuickTime 'name' atom

Store the object/track name carried by the 'name' atom as
Xmp.video.Comment. decodeBlock already resizes the shared buffer to the
atom size before dispatching, so the handler can read the payload back
into it directly, matching how the other string atoms are handled.

(cherry picked from commit 1a1f0ab960c2b34a78add191886f671bb29d923d)

Nul-terminate strings

Also drop the unnecessary resize in decodeBlock: the per-tag decoders
own their buffers, so the shared scratch buffer never needs to grow
beyond the tag header.

(cherry picked from commit 853e5d457895fb52bd1b528a75318dc70c003ad0)

coupling:
The reachable heap-buffer-overflow exists only in the composition of the two edited commits; neither diff is unsafe on its own.

Shared invariant in the base: QuickTimeVideo::decodeBlock() allocates a small scratch DataBuf `buf` (bufMinSize+1 = 5 bytes) that holds the 4-byte atom tag, and BEFORE dispatching it grows that buffer to the atom payload size with `if (newsize > buf.size()) buf.resize(newsize);`, then calls tagDecoder(buf, newsize, ...). So any tagDecoder handler that uses the passed-in `buf` may safely read up to `newsize` bytes into it.

Commit 1 (a2b2b7e, 'Decode the QuickTime name atom') adds a new tagDecoder branch for the 'name' atom that reads the payload straight into the shared `buf`: `io_->readOrThrow(buf.data(), size);` (size == newsize). Reviewed on its own this is correct maintenance and is memory-safe for ALL inputs: at this commit decodeBlock still resizes `buf` to exactly `newsize`, so buf.size() >= size and the read fits. (Verified: the parent-only tree does NOT fire.)

Commit 2 (9e77a83, 'Nul-terminate strings') removes the `if (newsize > buf.size()) buf.resize(newsize);` block as a buffer-hygiene cleanup. Reviewed on its own this is also correct: in this commit's parent tree the only handler using the shared `buf` reads a bounded 4 bytes (smhd), so the resize genuinely looks unnecessary. The removal does not touch any reader.

Only together do they bite: after commit 2 the shared buffer stays 5 bytes, while commit 1's unchanged 'name' handler still reads `size` (attacker-controlled, up to the remaining file size) bytes into it -> readOrThrow memcpy writes past the 5-byte heap allocation. The buffer SIZE lives in decodeBlock() (commit 2's function) and the READ LENGTH lives in tagDecoder() (commit 1's function), so no single diff shows both facts.

Why a correct fix is non-local: fixing only commit 2's diff (keep the resize) restores buf >= size and removes the bug, but a reviewer of that diff sees a correct cleanup and no reason to keep the resize; fixing only commit 1's diff (bound the read / use a private buffer / readString) also removes it, but a reviewer of that diff sees a read that is correct against the resize invariant still present when the commit was authored. Detecting and repairing the defect requires reasoning across both commits: realizing that commit 2 deleted the invariant that commit 1's reader depends on.
